recentItems.title: Talking Points: Is Ka Ying Rising The Best Sprinter We've Seen? | Luck On Sunday
recentItems.description:
Nick Luck is joined by Cornelius Lysaght and Eve Johnson Houghton for this week's Talking Points.

TripAdvisor has declined to list racing as a local attraction on welfare grounds, with Ripon among the courses affected. The BHA has written to them calling it surprising and troubling — the panel ask whether a firmer response is needed, and why bullfighting appears to be treated differently.

Also on the agenda: France Galop's proposed overhaul of the French fixture list, which could see several rural courses close; Constitution Hill rated 108 on the flat and what that leaves him; Ka Ying Rising's rating pushed up to 135 and whether the international panel has changed how it assesses champions; and Peter Savill stepping away from the ROA Council.

Plus a look ahead to the Arc, where Francis-Henri Graffard holds a strong hand, and Joseph O'Brien's ever-growing Melbourne Cup squad.

recentItems.description:
Live coverage from Leopardstown on Irish Champions Festival Saturday.

The Royal Bahrain Irish Champion Stakes is the feature, with Constitution River and Item meeting again after the Juddmonte International at York, alongside Almaqam, A Boy Named Susie, Hawk Mountain and Lambourne. 

Before that, Blue Bolt takes on the Ballydoyle pair Precise and True Love in the Coolmore America "Justify" Matron Stakes, and a big field goes to post for the Group 2 Solonaway Stakes.

recentItems.title: 50/1 SHOCK! Hotazhell Wins The Irish Champion Stakes 2026 | Replay | Racing TV
recentItems.description:
The form of the Grosser Dallmayr-Preis - Bayerisches Zuchtrennen in Munich really came to the fore in the Group 1 Royal Bahrain Irish Champion Stakes at Leopardstown as Hotazhell (50/1) held on by a nose from Wimbledon Hawkeye (33/1).

The pair clashed in that German Group 1 in July where Hotazhell prevailed with Wimbledon Hawkeye just over half a length away in third.

There was plenty going on in the straight in this 1.25m euro feature on day one of Irish Champions Festival with a number of horses running short of room.

Hotazhell was switched out to come with his challenge inside the final quarter of a mile and he took much closer order racing behind Constitution River at the furlong pole.

Hotazhell challenged and headed Constitution River in the closing stages, but he wasn't home yet as Wimbledon Hawkeye ran on powerfully to force the photograph in a thrilling finish.

The judge gave the verdict to Hotazhell by the narrowest margin from Wimbledon Hawkeye as 11/8 favourite Constitution River finished three-quarters of a length behind this battle in third.

recentItems.title: Quddwah Delivers In The Solonaway As James Doyle Doubles Up | Replay | Racing TV
recentItems.description:
Quddwah was another short-priced favourite to prevail on the opening day of Irish Champions Festival as he took the honours in the Group 2 Solonoway Stakes.

He tracked the leader Audience towards the straight and he was bustled and ridden by James Doyle to get the measure of the game leader a furlong down.

The even-money shot rolled home well in the closing stages to see it out by a length and a half from Audience (10/1).

Ed Crisford said: “He did it really well, it's nice to see him bounce back from his summer break.

“There wasn't much pace on and James put him in the prime posi.

“I thought he was a little bit rusty when James asked him, but he finished off really well.

“James is a super jockey and we like to use him a lot. He does really well for us and we've had a lot of success over the last few years with him.

“He's got the Daniel Wildenstein in France and there are races in America for him, there is a Grade 1 in October as well.

“I guess we'll just see how he is. He's won quite a few Grade 2s so it would be nice to give him a crack at a Grade 1.”

Doyle doubled up on Quddwah having also won the Kilternan Stakes on Arabian Crown (11/1).

Paddy Power halved Quddwah to 25/1 from 50/1 for the QEII.

recentItems.title: Blue Bolt Completes A Group 1 Treble In Three Countries | Replay | Racing TV
recentItems.description:
Blue Bolt made it a hat-trick of Group One victories, in three different countries, with an authoritative performance in the Matron Stakes at Leopardstown.

The 4/5 favourite was tanking along in a share of third behind Carolina Jetstream and Fallen Angel with fully three furlongs left.

The front pair began to exert their jockeys' arms on the turn in as Blue Bolt got a lovely split at the '2' pole.

She was given the office to lead charging to the final furlong and opened up in the final 100 yards to seal the first prize by two and a quarter lengths over City Of Memphis (9/1) with Fallen Angel in third at 8/1.

recentItems.title: Darkness Falls Is 10/1 For The Derby After Golden Fleece Glory | Replay | Racing TV
recentItems.description:
Darkness Falls came home strongly to both enhance his reputation and follow in the footsteps of some high-class Ballydoyle alumni in the HKJC World Pool Golden Fleece Stakes

Aidan O'Brien's youngster arrived at Leopardstown having impressed with a wide-margin success on his second start at the Curragh and relished tackling an extra furlong in a race run as a Group One for the first time, powering to a four-and-a-quarter-length win in the hands of Ryan Moore.

He adds his name to a roll of honour that includes Benvenuto Cellini (2025), Diego Velazquez (2023) and Auguste Rodin in recent years. He was made Paddy Power's 7-1 Derby favourite in the immediate aftermath.

O'Brien said of his even-money winner: “He had a lovely run around here in a maiden and then was very impressive the last day. Obviously he's by Camelot which makes him extra special.

“Ryan said the trip is going to be no problem, a mile and he's going to get a mile and a quarter next year. He's just has a lot of class.

“It's an unbelievable race to have on here at this time. It's a lovely first running of it. It's going to be a very important race and all the good horses were there, all the good middle-distance type horses.

“I was very impressed and delighted with him. It was a proper gallop, there was nowhere to hide out there. Ryan eased out with him and he quickened up very well.

“He has a lovely nature, which makes him really special. He's very exciting.

“He's out of a No Nay Never mare so there is a lot of speed in there but he has the class. I'm delighted to have him.”

On plans, O'Brien said: “I think he can go anywhere he wants. You can go to America with him at the end if you want, he's that type of horse.

“He's not going to need soft ground this horse, good fast ground.

“He's a Camelot that we thought was going to be a Guineas horse plus and that's the way his dad was.”
